pnpm verify exits 0 under the repo's 100% line/branch/function/statement thresholds with no ignore comment or config exclusion; every named clamp and key case has its own test and the 400 tests assert status and message. amendments.reason: The contract told me to comment that "the term 'on' also matches 'off'". That is false: 'off' does not contain 'on'. The repo's real rule (app.js indexOf over key+' '+type+' '+on|off) produces one quirk mechanism, not two: 'on' is a substring of 'config' and of keys like 'onboarding', which is WHY filtering 'on' returns flags that are off. Amended so the comment and tests state the true mechanism; the goal, the rubric and the 'two documented quirks' deliverable are unchanged and still met.
amendments.grounding: Verified mechanically: 'legacy boolean off'.includes('on') is false, 'pricing-config config off'.includes('on') is true. The roadmap's own discovery row (app.js live filter - exact semantics) carries the same incorrect claim.

changes: Add a short comment recording the two known quirks this rule keeps on purpose: the term 'on' also matches 'off', and 'on' also matches a key containing 'config'. Keeping them means no behaviour change for existing users.

Add a short comment recording the quirk this rule keeps on purpose: 'on' matches any flag whose key or type merely contains those letters (every 'config' flag, any key like 'onboarding'), so filtering 'on' also returns flags that are off. Note explicitly that 'off' does not contain 'on' - the overlap runs one way. Keeping it means no behaviour change for existing users.
